vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded API Key
vulnerabilities.description: API key is hardcoded in the source code, exposing sensitive credentials to anyone with code access.
vulnerabilities.risk: Credential exposure, unauthorized API access, potential account compromise

fix.description: Move API key to environment variables using .env file and python-dotenv
fix.implementation_details: Use python-dotenv to load environment variables from .env file at runtime

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection via String Formatting
vulnerabilities.description: User input is directly concatenated into SQL query using .format(), allowing SQL injection attacks.
vulnerabilities.code_snippet:
sql = "SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username LIKE '%{}%'".format(name)
cur.execute(sql)
vulnerabilities.risk: Database compromise, unauthorized data access, data manipulation or deletion

fix.description: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) with placeholders
fix.code_before:
sql = "SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username LIKE '%{}%'".format(name)
cur.execute(sql)
fix.code_after:
sql = "SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username LIKE ?"
cur.execute(sql, (f'%{name}%',))
fix.implementation_details: Replace .format() with parameterized query placeholders. SQLite uses '?' for placeholders.

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

vulnerabilities.title: Unsafe Pickle Deserialization (Remote Code Execution)
vulnerabilities.description: User-supplied data is deserialized using pickle.loads(), which can execute arbitrary code.
vulnerabilities.risk: Remote Code Execution (RCE), complete system compromise, arbitrary command execution

fix.description: Replace pickle with JSON deserialization and implement input validation
fix.code_after:
data = request.get_json()
if not isinstance(data, dict):
    return jsonify({"error": "Invalid request"}), 400
name = data.get("name", "")
if not isinstance(name, str) or len(name) > 255:
    return jsonify({"error": "Invalid name"}), 400
safe_name = escape(name)
fix.implementation_details: Use JSON format which is safe by design. Validate data types and lengths.

vulnerabilities.title: Command Injection via os.system()
vulnerabilities.description: User input is directly concatenated into shell commands using os.system(), allowing command injection.
vulnerabilities.risk: Remote Code Execution, arbitrary command execution, system compromise

fix.description: Use subprocess.run with shell=False and command whitelisting
fix.code_after:
allowed_commands = ['echo', 'date', 'whoami']
cmd_parts = cmd.strip().split()
if not cmd_parts or cmd_parts[0] not in allowed_commands:
    return jsonify({"error": "Command not allowed"}), 403
subprocess.run(cmd_parts, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
fix.implementation_details: Use subprocess.run with shell=False to prevent injection. Whitelist allowed commands.

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

vulnerabilities.title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
vulnerabilities.description: User input is directly inserted into template strings passed to render_template_string().
vulnerabilities.risk: Template Injection attacks, potential code execution via Jinja2 expressions

fix.description: Avoid render_template_string with user input. Use proper templating or JSON responses.
fix.implementation_details: Use escape() from Werkzeug or return JSON. Never use user input in template strings.

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Templating Engine

vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded Plain Text Passwords
vulnerabilities.description: User passwords are stored as plain text in the USERS dictionary, visible in source code.
vulnerabilities.risk: Credential exposure, unauthorized account access, password compromise

fix.implementation_details: Use bcrypt or PBKDF2-based hashing. Store only hashes, never plain text passwords.

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

vulnerabilities.title: Plain Text Password Comparison
vulnerabilities.description: Authentication uses direct string comparison without timing attack protection or proper hashing.
vulnerabilities.risk: Timing attacks, weak password verification, no session management

fix.code_before:
if user and user.get("password") == password:
    return "login ok"
fix.implementation_details: Use check_password_hash() which performs constant-time comparison. Add logging for security events.

vulnerabilities.title: Debug Mode Enabled in Production
vulnerabilities.description: Flask debug mode is hardcoded to True, exposing sensitive information and enabling code execution.
vulnerabilities.risk: Information disclosure, error stack traces leaking sensitive data, interactive debugger access

fix.description: Load debug mode from environment variables, default to False
fix.implementation_details: Always default to False. Only enable in development environment via environment variable.

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-215: Information Exposure Through Debug Information

vulnerabilities.title: Lack of Error Handling and Logging
vulnerabilities.description: No structured error handling, logging, or input validation throughout the application.
vulnerabilities.code_snippet: No error handlers or logging setup
vulnerabilities.risk: Information disclosure via error messages, inability to detect attacks, poor incident response

fix.description: Implement comprehensive logging and error handling
fix.code_before: # No logging or structured error handling
fix.implementation_details: Add logging for security events and errors. Implement proper error handlers that don't leak sensitive information.

vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

immediate_actions: Replace all hardcoded credentials with environment variables
Fix all SQL injection vulnerabilities by using parameterized queries
Remove pickle deserialization and replace with JSON
Implement password hashing for all stored credentials
security_best_practices: Use environment variables for all sensitive configuration
Implement input validation and sanitization for all user inputs
Use parameterized queries for all database operations
Never trust user input - escape/validate everything
Implement rate limiting for authentication endpoints
Regular security audits and penetration testing
